content: Sulfamethoxazole, marketed as BACTRIM, has specific dosage and administration guidelines depending on the condition being treated and the age of the patient. Below are the detailed instructions for its use: 1. Contraindication in Pediatric Patients Under 2 Months of Age: BACTRIM is contraindicated in children younger than 2 months due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 2. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) and Shigellosis: Adults: The standard dosage for adults treating urinary tract infections is either one BACTRIM DS (double strength) tablet or two regular BACTRIM tablets every 12 hours. This regimen is continued for 10 to 14 days. For shigellosis, the same dosage is administered daily but for a duration of 5 days. Children: For pediatric patients with urinary tract infections or acute otitis media, the recommended dose is 40 mg/kg of sulfamethoxazole and 8 mg/kg of trimethoprim per 24 hours. This total daily dose is divided into two doses, administered every 12 hours, and continued for 10 days. For shigellosis, the same daily dosage is used but for 5 days. 3. Acute Otitis Media in Children: The dosing for children with acute otitis media follows the same guidelines as for urinary tract infections, with 40 mg/kg of sulfamethoxazole and 8 mg/kg of trimethoprim per 24 hours, divided into two doses every 12 hours for 10 days. 4. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis in Adults: Adults experiencing acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis are prescribed one BACTRIM DS tablet or two regular BACTRIM tablets every 12 hours for a total of 14 days. 5. Pneumocystis Jiroveci Pneumonia (Treatment): Adults and Children: For confirmed cases of Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia, the recommended dosage is 75 to 100 mg/kg of sulfamethoxazole and 15 to 20 mg/kg of trimethoprim per 24 hours. This total daily dose is divided into four equal doses, administered every 6 hours, and continued for 14 to 21 days. For the lower limit of the dose (75 mg/kg sulfamethoxazole and 15 mg/kg trimethoprim per 24 hours), 75% of the upper limit dose is administered. 6. Pneumocystis Jiroveci Pneumonia (Prophylaxis): Adults: For prophylaxis in adults, the recommended dose is one BACTRIM DS tablet taken once daily. Children: For pediatric prophylaxis, the recommended dose is 750 mg/m²/day of sulfamethoxazole and 150 mg/m²/day of trimethoprim. This dose is divided into two equal doses, administered twice daily, on three consecutive days per week. The total daily dose should not exceed 1600 mg of sulfamethoxazole and 320 mg of trimethoprim. 7. Traveler’s Diarrhea in Adults: For adults treating traveler’s diarrhea, the standard dosage is one BACTRIM DS tablet or two regular BACTRIM tablets every 12 hours for a duration of 5 days. These dosing regimens are designed to optimize therapeutic outcomes while minimizing the risk of adverse effects. It is essential to adhere strictly to the prescribed dosages and durations for each specific condition.
